clinician.final_diagnosis: A tension pneumothorax, possibly secondary to underlying COVID-19
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 36-year-old man presented with a 3-week history of dry cough, fever, and worsening breathlessness, culminating in acute hypoxaemia and left-sided chest signs. Chest X-ray confirmed a large left-sided tension pneumothorax with mediastinal shift. Initial treatment with emergency needle decompression led to immediate clinical and radiological improvement, followed by insertion of a chest drain. Follow-up imaging showed lung re-expansion but extensive bilateral consolidation. SARS-CoV-2 PCR was initially negative; however, clinical suspicion of COVID-19 remained high based on history and imaging. No prior trauma or lung disease was documented. Microbiological confirmation was unavailable. The clinical course and response to treatment support the diagnosis of tension pneumothorax, likely secondary to underlying COVID-19.
